ANNEX A [ Clause 3.2, Table 1, Item ( i ) ]
DETERMINATION A-l PRINCIPLE
Benomyl is extracted by dissolving in chloroform and filtration employing a millipore filter. The linear absorbance of the infra-red light source is measured at the 1140 cm-1 wavenumber ( considered to be a stretching frequency involving the ester grouping ) and the concentration of benomyl is calculated relative to a predetermined absorbance value of a reference standard.

OF BENOMYL CONTENT A-4.2 Preparation of Sample Solution Weigh accurately a quantity of sample so as to contain 0'22 g becomyl and prepare the solution following the same procedure as has been described in A-4.1.
NOTE - The solution may be centrifuged for 2 minutes before filtering for obtaining accurate results. It will be essential to do this exercise in cases where benomyl content is less than 50 percent by mass.

A-2 APPARATUS A-2.1 In&a-red Spectrophotometer A-2.2 Absorption Cells Scdium chloride cells having path of about 0'20 mm. A-2.3 Hypodermic 1 ml capacity. A-2.4 Mechanical Shaker A-2.5 Millipore Filter A-2.6 Filter Discs Millipore 13 mm, pore size 0.45 p. Syringe an internal light

A-4.3 Calibration A-4.3.1 Fill an absorption cell with chloroform. Adjust the spectrophotometer for the optimum instrument setting with respect to gain, slit width, response, speed and drum drive. Make scan with chloroform in the cell over the wavelength region 1180 cm-l to 1120 cm-l. A-4.3.2 Turn the wavelength scale back to its original setting. Fill the cell with reference standard solution ( A-4.1 ). Make a scan in the to 1120 cm-l wavelength region 1180 cm-l with the same setting as previously used ( A-4.3.1 ). Determine the linear absorbance of the solution at 1140 cm-l using chloroform blank absorbance as the baseline. A-4.3.3 Turn the wavelength scale back to its original setting. Fill the cell with sample solution ( A-4.2 ). Make a scan in the wavelength region 1180 cm-l to 1120 cm-l, with the same setting as previously used (A-4.3.1 ). Determine the linear absorbance of the solution at 1140 cm-l using chloroform blank absorbance as the baseline. A-5 CALCULATION Benomyl content, A X 25 x 100 percent by mass = M x Bx where A = peak absorbance at ] 140 cm-1 - absorbance. of chloroform blaKk at 1140 cm-l ; M = mass, in g, of sample taken for the test;
B =

A-2.7 Specimen Bottles 25 x 95 mm size and with screw caps. A-3 REAGENTS A-3.1 Basic Alumina A-3.2 Chloroform A-3.3 Reference Standard Benomyl Of known purity. A-4 PROCEDURE A-4.1 Preparation of Reference Standard Solution Weigh about 0.22 g reference standard. benomyl in a specimen bottle and accurately add 25 ml chloroform and immediately close tightly with a screw cap. Clamp the vial to a mechanical shaker and shake for 5 minutes. Allow the solution to stand for 4 more minutes. With the aid of a 1 ml syringe, filter the solution through the millipore filter into the absorption cell.

Standard Mark
I

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained-from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Bureau of Indian Standards BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Sfundizrds Act, 2986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. Copyright BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, types or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS. Review of Indian Standards Amendments are issued io standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards Monthly Additions'.
